title: A local governor is founded and seated at Qurṭuba, the old seat of the caliphs, to carry the crown's authority up and down the great river through the lands won in 1349
The amir marries his Marīnid bride, Duʿāʾ, fulfilling the betrothal agreed with the house of Fās in January 1348
The amir marries his Ḥafṣid bride, Tizemt, fulfilling the betrothal agreed with Tūnis in July 1345: his third wife, and his second bride from the Maghrib in three months

The Ghana betrothal is fulfilled, though not as the court intended: Faraj ibn Ismāʿīl, the amir's elder brother and lately his regent, marries Fatiu, daughter of the old ruler of Ghana, and goes south across the desert to live in her land
source: Trent's account (the exact date isn't given; reported by 19 November 1355)
